neutral_facts.value: The accused, who was living with the victim and her children, was involved in an altercation with the victim on the night of the incident. The victim was heard crying and was seen being taken away by the accused towards another person's house. Later, the victim's body was found hanging from a tree. The accused did not report the victim's disappearance or inform the police, and no reasonable explanation was provided for the victim's death. The prosecution relied on circumstantial evidence, including the accused's failure to report the incident and the victim's last seen alive with the accused.

investigation_status.value: Charge sheet filed, FIR registered, trial completed

quotes.text: Statement of PW -1 was recorded, based on which, case in FIR No.250 of 2007 was registered under Section 302 IPC and Section 201 read with Section 34 IPC.
Upon completion of investigation, chargesheet was filed against accused Raj Kumar, Ramesh Kumar, Om Prakash and Barfi Devi under Section 302 IPC and Section 201 read with Section 34 IPC.
The trial court convicted the respondent-accused under Section 302 IPC and Section 201 IPC read with Section 34 IPC and sentenced him to undergo imprisonment for life.
The High Court allowed the criminal appeal filed by the respondent-accused thereby setting aside the conviction and the sentence of life imprisonment imposed upon him.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution case is based on circumstantial evidence, which must be cogent, reliable, and form a complete chain pointing to the guilt of the accused. The circumstances are consistent with the hypothesis of the accused's guilt and inconsistent with his innocence. The deceased was last seen alive with the accused, and he failed to provide a satisfactory explanation for her disappearance and death.

quotes.text: Prosecution case is based on circumstantial evidence. It is well settled that in a case based on circumstantial evidence, the circumstances from which an inference of guilt is sought to be drawn must be cogently and firmly established and that those circumstances must be conclusive in nature unerringly pointing towards the guilt of the accused.

The circumstances relied upon by the prosecution are proved by cogent and reliable evidence. The circumstances cumulatively taken form a complete chain pointing out that the murder was committed by the accused and none-else.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the prosecution's case suffered from serious infirmities, including the alleged improvements in the testimony of PW-1, which made him an unreliable witness. They also suggested that the deceased may have committed suicide by consuming poison.

quotes.text: The High Court observed that Jeewan Lal (PW-1) son of the deceased, while deposing as witness before the court in narrating the whole incident, had made improvements and hence, PW-1 is not a reliable witness.
A feeble attempt was made by the defence to suggest that the deceased consumed poison and committed suicide.

legal_principle_applied.value: The court applied the principle that in cases based on circumstantial evidence, the circumstances must be cogently and firmly established, form a complete chain, and be inconsistent with the accused's innocence. The burden of proof lies on the accused to explain the circumstances.

quotes.text: In a case based on circumstantial evidence, the inference of guilt can be drawn only when all the incriminating facts and circumstances are found to be incompatible with the innocence of the accused.
In view of Section 106 of the Evidence Act, burden is cast upon the accused, being the inmate of the house to give a cogent explanation as to how the deceased died.

judicial_aggravating_factors.value: The accused failed to provide a satisfactory explanation for the deceased's death, and his failure to report the missing of the deceased is a strong militating circumstance against him.

quotes.text: The accused has no reasonable explanation as to how the body of the deceased was found hanging from the tree. It is for the accused to explain as to what happened to the deceased.

The accused being inmate of the house cannot get away by simply keeping quiet and offering no explanation. This is a strong militating circumstance against the respondent indicating that he might be responsible for the commission of the offence.
